ledger.note: 1814: Cliopatria restarts the Zaydi imamate of Sana'a. The Qasimid state, 'also known as the Imamate of Yemen' (founded 1597, Qasimid page), lost its coast to the Wahhabis after 1803; the Imams of Yemen page lists al-Mutawakkil Ahmad (1809-1816) as imam, so the imamate never lapsed. The pages do not say why Cliopatria's row starts in 1814; bridging at confidence 1.

sources.title: Qasimid state
sources.note: The Qasimid state 'also known as the Imamate of Yemen'; coast lost after 1803, regained temporarily 1818, 1833.

notes: Same state, two Cliopatria rows: the Qasimid state (1597-1849 on Wikipedia, 'also known as the Imamate of Yemen') is the Zaydi imamate of Sana'a; Cliopatria has Qasimids 1636-1802 (Q5261548, another group's dossier qasimids) and Imamate of Yemen 1814-1872 (Q1042069). They are written as two dossiers, linked as predecessor and successor; the colour agent should give them one colour. Not a founding in 1814: no page dates it (found event at confidence 1). The imamate did not end in 1872: the imams (al-Mutawakkil al-Muhsin 1855-1878, al-Hadi Sharaf ad-Din 1878-1890, al-Mansur Muhammad 1890-1904) kept Upper Yemen under formal Ottoman recognition and revolted again in 1904-05; a dossier for the highlands imamate 1873-1918 is missing (suggested slug imamate-of-upper-yemen; Cliopatria has no row between 1873 and 1918). Cliopatria draws the Tihama coast inside the imamate throughout; the pages say it was lost after 1803, regained temporarily in 1818, lost to Egypt in 1833 and then taken by the Ottomans in 1849; the corrected keyframes remove it. Not settled: who held the coast in 1840-1848 (pages silent; the Egyptian withdrawal is undated), the extent the imam held in the north (Sa'dah, Jizan and Najran are in Cliopatria's 1815 shape and on no page), and why the shape grows in 1815. The ledger's 1833 loss to muhammad-ali-dynasty has no mirror gain in that dossier (its Cliopatria shapes never included the Yemeni coast; a gap-filler should add it from the Yemen Eyalet page). The Ottoman dossier dates its Yemen gain 1873 (Cliopatria's year) against 1872 here. No ruler strip: the Imams of Yemen page says 'There is no uncontroversial list of imams of Yemen' and its list has overlapping reigns (for example al-Mansur Muhammad bin Abdallah 1853-1890 and al-Mutawakkil al-Muhsin 1855-1878). Area: no infobox figure on any page (the Yemen Vilayet page gives about 200,000 km2 for the vilayet in 1900, a different entity).
